related_questions.question: What are the risks of the COVID vaccine?

text_blocks.snippet: The most common risks associated with COVID-19 vaccines are relatively minor and temporary, such as pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, and nausea. More serious, but rare, risks include anaphylaxis, a severe allergic reaction, and myocarditis or pericarditis, inflammation of the heart muscle or surrounding lining, according to the CDC. These serious reactions are rare, and healthcare professionals are equipped to manage them effectively, according to the CDC.
snippet_highlighted_words: pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, and nausea

list.snippet: Pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site: These are very common and usually subside within a few days.
Fatigue: Many people experience tiredness after vaccination.
Headache: Headaches are another common side effect.
Muscle pain: Some individuals may experience muscle aches.
Chills: A feeling of coldness with shivering can occur.
Fever: A slight fever is also possible.
Nausea: Some people may feel queasy.

list.title: Anaphylaxis:
list.snippet: This is a severe allergic reaction that can occur after any vaccine, but it is very rare with COVID-19 vaccines according to the CDC. Symptoms include wheezing, difficulty breathing, low blood pressure, or hives. It requires immediate treatment with epinephrine.

list.title: Myocarditis and Pericarditis:
list.snippet: These are rare instances of inflammation of the heart muscle or the lining around the heart, according to the CDC. They are more commonly reported in younger males, particularly after mRNA vaccines, according to the CDC.
